TRANSPORT CROOK

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a transport broker reels in deals, hires sub-contracts and makes off with all the money.

Unique Selling Point:
CLASSIC CROOK

Summary:
Elsie Labuschangne has been running transport cons for years – she’s a professional crook.

The MO is simple – get a contract from a mining company to move goods, then get a sub-contractor to the work, while she collects the cash without paying the sub contractor.

We’re talking losses in excess of R6 million. Police cases have been opened – but Elsie is still operating with her two latest victims in July.


Further information:
CASE STUDY 1:
Norman - TRUCK OWNER
He got caught in July when he did one load with four trucks for her – he used one of his own trucks and sub-contracted the other three.
THE LOSS: R34 000 – he has paid the other three truck owners from his own pocket.
ACTION: Criminal case opened

CASE STUDY 2:
Alridge Coetzee – TRANSPORTER (KIMBERLY)
Alridge did work for her over a period of three months during 2014/2015 at three different mines. Hired in other transporters to help with the contracts. He subsequently contacted the mines – two refused to give out information saying they’ve entered into an agreement with Elsie. The third company provided proof of payment made to Elsie.
THE LOSS: He personally lost R600 000 and had to close down his business. He estimates that the other transporters lost in the region of R3 million (documentation to be emailed tonight). Alridge is also still paying back some of the transporters he employed.
ACTION: Criminal case opened, tried to pursue the it legally

CASE STUDY 3:
Jaques van Rensburg – TRANSPORTER
Did work in 2014 – lost R500 000. Had to close down – lost all his trucks
He has organised a group of transporters that have been done in by her and has kept a record of the companies she has defrauded.

I have a list of 8 others – some who contracted additional trucks to do the work for Elsie. List totals – over R5 million.

METAL DEALER - KASHINKA DHAR
Mr. Dhar awarded Elsie a contract to transport goods for him R140 per ton in July this year. She contracted Norman and a second transporter Pierre Brink (he lost R150k but is in Rustenburg) at a rate of R240 per ton – she would never be able to pay that if she wasn’t earning that. Mr. Dhar will do an interview – he has all the proof of payments he made to her. He was impressed because the job was done quickly and efficiently without any hassles – little did he know Elsie was a fraudster.

WHAT WE HAVE:
- Bankstatement to show money coming into her personal bank account and being withdrawn.
- She used a company’s details, but gave her own personal bank account for payment.
- Proof that she was offered one rate per ton from the mine and then inflated it to lure sub-contractors

SAPS INTERVIEW
Cases have been opened since 2014 – but Elsie is still a free agent ripping off all and sundry.

ROAD FREIGHT ASSOCIATION
Brokers are the middlemen that often take advantage of transporters – fraud is huge and the industry unregulated.

Press Release:


Transport Crook
It’s an easy con – pull in the deals, get subcontractors to do all the work, pocket the big bucks and disappear without
paying. That’s how one middleman in the transport industry almost got away with stealing millions from
transporters. Carte Blanche tracks down this elusive scamster.

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT

VO: Over R456 billion worth of goods, gets moved across South African roads every year.

The transport industry is big business. And a lot of people want in on the action – opening the door to corruption.

LINK: There are many role players – clients, transporters and middlemen known as brokers – and these brokers that are often at the centre of dodgy deals.

NORMAN: I actually did the work and never got paid for it.
PIERRE: We didn’t get paid.
CHARL: There’s in excess of 90% at least of the monies outstanding

VO: All three these businessmen dealt with transport broker Elsie Labuschagne from Bela-Bela in Limpopo – their losses total over R3.1 million .

They are not the only ones that appear to have been conned by Elsie says Private Investigator Chad Thomas. He investigated her in 2015.

CHAD: we found that our client was literally one of dozens of people that had been taken. // All the people that came forward had the same story to tell – they had lost money –they were all subcontractors and they were supplying a transport service.

VO: Chad says the modus operandi is pretty basic.

CHAD: She would go to a company or an organisation requiring transport –and she would come in at very good rate // she would then farm it out at a higher rate // she would never have been in a position to settle everybody.

VO: Charl Oberholzer was contracted by Elsie Labuschagne in 2014 – his company transported loads for her over a period of three months.

CHARL: She made a couple of very small insignificant payments to us, even though by that time she owing in the millions.

VO: The cargo owners were big reputable companies – he says there was no reason to doubt Elsie.

CHARL: The paperwork seemed to be legitimate and even the people we dealt with on ground level were all legitimate people.


VO: But when payments weren’t forth coming for the work done, Charl pulled his trucks off sight.

DEVI: Did she ask why you stopped?
CHARL: No she just basically disappears. There’s not even a… any question of why’re stopping the trucks. It’s as if she expects it.

LINK: We traced Elsie Labuschagne to Bela-Bela, we hear that she is lying very low – but I’m going to try and find her.

VO: After checking some of the addresses listed for Elsie, we eventually got her on the phone.

UPSOUND CALL
ELSIE: Apparently you also think I am in Bela-Bela
DEVI: I know you are in Bela-Bela.
ELSIE: No, I’m not in Bela-Bela.

VO: Strike one Elsie. Realising we were on to her, she agreed to meet us.

DEVI: Why did you lie to me // When I knew you were here.
ELSIE: So many people say they from carte blanche, from this and this…
DEVI: Elsie, there are a lot of people that are very unhappy with you , they say that as a transport broker you defrauded them and you owe them a lot of money and in some cases millions?
ELSIE: There’s no such thing that I am owing them millions.

VO: Strike two Elsie.

We called 19 transporters – who claim they’ve collectively lost over R20 million in jobs done through Elsie – some dating back to 2008, many have left the transport industry unable to recover from the financial loss.

But Elsie claimed it’s not her fault – she is also owed a lot of money.

CHAD: One the majority of her contracts she was in fact paid. She sent us correspondence where she was claimed to be owed 2.5 million rand one particular contract //– what about all the other money that should have come in?

VO: In Charl’s case – although she is owed some money. Bank statements showed that Elsie actually received R1.1 million for the services rendered by Charl’s company.

DEVI: Did you get money from anybody for any of the work that was done by Charl Oberholzer?
ELSIE: yes I did.
DEVI: how much did you get?
ELSIE That I’ll have to tell you in total, it was about I would say a million
DEVI: Charl’s claim is that you only him R265000
ELSIE: No we paid him more

VO: A claim she could not prove.

Collecting money from clients, and not paying sub-contractors in full seems to be a pattern for Elsie.

In July, Transporter Norman Liwanda and Logistics Project Manager Pierre Brink both had contracts, in Rustenburg, through Elsie’s company.

When payment wasn’t forth coming they both stopped sending their trucks.

PIERRE: I spoke to the client, //he sent me the proof of payments as well as the invoices that Elsie has sent to him and that is when I made the calculation that the rates is completely off, because her invoices was significantly lower than what mine was.

VO: It would appear that Elsie was inflating rates to draw in transporters .

NORMAN: The client indicated that he had never agreed to pay Elsie 220 per ton. // It was at that point in time again that I realised that there was something that was not right here, because there was nowhere that the… Elsie was going to pay the difference for the client if the client was offering 175.

VO: A number of other victims all say they were offered inflated rates by Elsie as well.

LINK: But why would anyone offer a deal like that – paying out more than you’re getting in – it doesn’t make any business sense.

VO: Elsie claimed the shortfall would come from her 30% commission.

DEIV: Even if you work on 30% of the total value of the deal – you still would not have been able to pay the difference.
ELSIE: ja, I’m guilty of that.
DEVI: so, you would offer enticing deals so that they couldn’t say no.
ELSIE: Ja, I am guilty of that.

VO: In Norman’s case he supplied delivery notes and invoiced for R34 000, Elsie paid R16 000 of that upfront.

NORMAN: there is communication that she sent via email to confirm that she received my invoice and she was working on it and as soon as she received payment from her client, she is going to pay me.

DEVI: In Norman’s case did you get your money in this case?
ELSIE: I didn’t get all my money

VO: Strike three Elsie. This is proof of payment from the client that paid her for the work done by Norman.

DEVI: Didn’t you or didn’t you get paid?
ELSIE: ja, I got paid – there it is.
DEVI: so where is norman’s money?
ELSIE: It’s still in my account.
DEVI: Elsie, what is wrong… why are you lying?
……. Why when I ask you, you give me one answer and when I show you proof you give me another answer?
ELSIE: Can I explain to you, You know why I am scared to open this…. In 2010 – involved with people who to our offices who wanted to shoot us because people never paid us.
DEVI: How is that Norman’s problem?
ELSIE: No that’s not Norman’s problem. That’s an old case.

VO: Chad says Elsie she presented similar irrelevant excuses before.

CHAD: She first advised us she had medical problems // and when that didn’t work she came with the story she was the victim in a conspiracy where other transport companies were trying to force her out of the industry. Elsie played the victim all along.

VO: While Elsie tried that with us as well. She couldn’t get around the facts.

In Pierre’s case, Elsie was paid at least R40 000, she in turn only paid him 25 of the R145 000 invoiced.

This is the invoice she sent through to the client. Note the VAT charged by Elsie.

DEVI: Are you charging VAT?
ELSIE: yes I do.
DEVI: you are charging VAT under Concordia?
ELSIE: ja
DEVI: Why?
ELSIE: because I thought it is going to be…. It’s not right…
DEVI: Elsie, does Concordia have a VAT number?
ELSIE: They are busy…
DEVI: ah, ah….
ELSIE: No not yet.
DEVI: Ok, just explain to me – what is this and that VAT amount there – just explain to me – I may have this completely wrong.
ELSIE: that’s my mistake.
DEVI: Are you crazy?
ELSIE: Yes.
DEVI: That’s Fruad
ELSIE: I know…

VO: Elsie has already had a run in with the law – she was found guilty of fraud in a different matter in 2008.

dEVI: you don’t think you’ve got a fraud problem.
ELSIE: ja, it seems to be I have a fraud problem. Now the people are taking that , do you know they make a big thing of fraud – now she’s always got fraud, fraud, - she’s always doing the wrong thing.
DEVI: you don’t think you’re proving it all by yourself?
ELSIE: Ja, I think so.

VO: But getting the authorities to prove it, is proving difficult.

In 2015, Charl opened a criminal case with the Commercial Crimes Unit in Pretoria. But the state advocate dealing with case steered him in a different direction.

CHARL: He told us that he felt that this was a civil matter // He actually nolly prosecuted the case and refused to prosecute.

VO: The civil case against Elsie and the company she claimed to be operating would shed new light on her dodgy dealings.

She was not a director of the company and the bank account she used to invoice on behalf of the business – was in fact in her personal name.

CHARL: We found that the accounts were empty, that there were no assets registered on her name.

LINK: There is a point when a civil case becomes criminal and it would seem that Elsie Labuschagne may have crossed that line

ANDILE: It’s a very clear case of fraud – which should give rise to a criminal case.

VO: Attorney Andile Nikani says this could fly as a criminal case.

ANDILE: it’s not a once off incident where one can claim a mistake – not any where is she claiming that work was never done, the work was done. // She simply doesn’t pay // which shows right from the beginning that she had what the court would define to be a wilful perversion of the truth

VO: The criminal case has been reopened.

When Elsie eventually ran out of excuses she turned on the water works.

DEVI: Are they picking on you?
ELSIE: Yah, they’re picking on me….
DEVI: We’ve spoken to 19 people – all the same story.
ELSIE: No devi, there was a lindy du Preez – want to see me in jail

VO: She’s absolutely right a lot of people want to see her behind bars.

DEVI: What see happen?
CHARL: For her to be locked away for a very, very long time. [Indistinct] protecting South Africa by doing that. //I think Elsie Labuschagne, what I see is only the tip of the ice berg.


PROMOS

PROMO 1
CHARL: I think Elsie Labuschagne, what I see is only the tip of the ice berg.

VO: We expose a transport broker who allegedly made millions in dodgy deals.

PROMO 2
VO: A transport industry broker who stands accused of stealing over R20 million from sub-contractors – has been ducking and diving – we track her down.

ELSIE: Apparently you also think I am in Bela-Bela
DEVI: I know you are in Bela-Bela.

PROMO 3
VO: A group of transporters across South Africa claim they’ve been defrauded by the same broker who appears to have a track record when it comes to dodgy deals.

DEVI: You would offer enticing deals so that they couldn’t say no.
ELSIE: Ja, I am guilty of that.

DEVI: That’s Fruad ELSIE: I know… VO: Elsie has already had a run in with the law – she was found guilty of fraud in a different matter in 2008. dEVI: you don’t think you’ve got a fraud problem. ELSIE: ja, it seems to be I have a fraud problem. Now the people are taking that , do you know they make a big thing of fraud – now she’s always got fraud, fraud, - she’s always doing the wrong thing. DEVI: you don’t think you’re proving it all by yourself? ELSIE: Ja, I think so. VO: But getting the authorities to prove it, is proving difficult. In 2015, Charl opened a criminal case with the Commercial Crimes Unit in Pretoria. But the state advocate dealing with case steered him in a different direction. CHARL: He told us that he felt that this was a civil matter // He actually nolly prosecuted the case and refused to prosecute. VO: The civil case against Elsie and the company she claimed to be operating would shed new light on her dodgy dealings. She was not a director of the company and the bank account she used to invoice on behalf of the business – was in fact in her personal name. CHARL: We found that the accounts were empty, that there were no assets registered on her name. LINK: There is a point when a civil case becomes criminal and it would seem that Elsie Labuschagne may have crossed that line ANDILE: It’s a very clear case of fraud – which should give rise to a criminal case. VO: Attorney Andile Nikani says this could fly as a criminal case. ANDILE: it’s not a once off incident where one can claim a mistake – not any where is she claiming that work was never done, the work was done. // She simply doesn’t pay // which shows right from the beginning that she had what the court would define to be a wilful perversion of the truth VO: The criminal case has been reopened. When Elsie eventually ran out of excuses she turned on the water works. DEVI: Are they picking on you? ELSIE: Yah, they’re picking on me…. DEVI: We’ve spoken to 19 people – all the same story. ELSIE: No devi, there was a lindy du Preez – want to see me in jail VO: She’s absolutely right a lot of people want to see her behind bars. DEVI: What see happen? CHARL: For her to be locked away for a very, very long time. [Indistinct] protecting South Africa by doing that. //I think Elsie Labuschagne, what I see is only the tip of the ice berg. PROMOS PROMO 1 CHARL: I think Elsie Labuschagne, what I see is only the tip of the ice berg. VO: We expose a transport broker who allegedly made millions in dodgy deals. PROMO 2 VO: A transport industry broker who stands accused of stealing over R20 million from sub-contractors – has been ducking and diving – we track her down. ELSIE: Apparently you also think I am in Bela-Bela DEVI: I know you are in Bela-Bela. PROMO 3 VO: A group of transporters across South Africa claim they’ve been defrauded by the same broker who appears to have a track record when it comes to dodgy deals. DEVI: You would offer enticing deals so that they couldn’t say no. ELSIE: Ja, I am guilty of that.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose a transport broker reels in deals, hires sub-contracts and makes off with all the money.
metadata.Summary: Elsie Labuschangne has been running transport cons for years – she’s a professional crook. The MO is simple – get a contract from a mining company to move goods, then get a sub-contractor to the work, while she collects the cash without paying the sub contractor. We’re talking losses in excess of R6 million. Police cases have been opened – but Elsie is still operating with her two latest victims in July.
metadata.Further information: CASE STUDY 1: Norman - TRUCK OWNER He got caught in July when he did one load with four trucks for her – he used one of his own trucks and sub-contracted the other three. THE LOSS: R34 000 – he has paid the other three truck owners from his own pocket. ACTION: Criminal case opened CASE STUDY 2: Alridge Coetzee – TRANSPORTER (KIMBERLY) Alridge did work for her over a period of three months during 2014/2015 at three different mines. Hired in other transporters to help with the contracts. He subsequently contacted the mines – two refused to give out information saying they’ve entered into an agreement with Elsie. The third company provided proof of payment made to Elsie. THE LOSS: He personally lost R600 000 and had to close down his business. He estimates that the other transporters lost in the region of R3 million (documentation to be emailed tonight). Alridge is also still paying back some of the transporters he employed. ACTION: Criminal case opened, tried to pursue the it legally CASE STUDY 3: Jaques van Rensburg – TRANSPORTER Did work in 2014 – lost R500 000. Had to close down – lost all his trucks He has organised a group of transporters that have been done in by her and has kept a record of the companies she has defrauded. I have a list of 8 others – some who contracted additional trucks to do the work for Elsie. List totals – over R5 million. METAL DEALER - KASHINKA DHAR Mr. Dhar awarded Elsie a contract to transport goods for him R140 per ton in July this year. She contracted Norman and a second transporter Pierre Brink (he lost R150k but is in Rustenburg) at a rate of R240 per ton – she would never be able to pay that if she wasn’t earning that. Mr. Dhar will do an interview – he has all the proof of payments he made to her. He was impressed because the job was done quickly and efficiently without any hassles – little did he know Elsie was a fraudster. WHAT WE HAVE: - Bankstatement to show money coming into her personal bank account and being withdrawn. - She used a company’s details, but gave her own personal bank account for payment. - Proof that she was offered one rate per ton from the mine and then inflated it to lure sub-contractors SAPS INTERVIEW Cases have been opened since 2014 – but Elsie is still a free agent ripping off all and sundry. ROAD FREIGHT ASSOCIATION Brokers are the middlemen that often take advantage of transporters – fraud is huge and the industry unregulated.
